description: EQUIPO DE ESTUDIANTES EN UN PROGRMA DE POSGRADO INTERESADOS EN EL DESARROLLO E INOVACION DE PROYECTOS PARA RESOLVER PROBLEMATICAS AMBINTALES.
summary: We propose the development of an intelligent digital tool that integrates NASA satellite observations, meteorological data, and physicochemical soil properties to design and evaluate crop rotation strategies adapted to the environmental conditions of each agricultural region. Through geospatial analysis and multi-criteria optimization models, the system will analyze variables such as soil moisture, temperature, precipitation, water availability, nutrients, and agricultural history. Using this information, it generates crop rotation scenarios that allow comparing their productivity, water-use efficiency, and contribution to soil conservation. This proposal aims to strengthen the resilience of agricultural systems in the face of climate change, reduce soil degradation, optimize the use of water resources, and provide decision-support tools for farmers. Furthermore, it promotes the use of satellite data, emerging technologies, and artificial intelligence to drive a more sustainable and adaptive agriculture.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Our project consists of developing a smart agriculture digital platform that uses artificial intelligence, NASA satellite observations, and local soil data to identify agricultural areas affected by droughts, heavy rainfall, soil erosion, and land degradation. Farmers enter information about their land, including its geographical location, soil type, pH, organic matter, water availability, and previous or desired crops. The system analyzes this information along with satellite data from Landsat, MODIS, SMAP, GPM, NASA POWER, ECOSTRESS, GRACE-FO, and SRTM. Artificial intelligence processes these variables to generate sustainable crop rotation recommendations adapted to the environmental conditions of each region.

2. What benefits does it have?

The project offers several benefits. It helps farmers make better agricultural decisions, optimize water use, reduce soil erosion, improve soil fertility, and maintain agricultural productivity. It also promotes sustainable practices such as minimum tillage, cover crops, crop rotation, and the use of organic matter. Additionally, it can help farmers anticipate climate-related risks and adapt their agricultural activities to changing environmental conditions.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The main goal is to contribute to more sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture. We aim to reduce soil degradation, protect natural resources, improve crop production, and support farmers who face environmental challenges. In the long term, this project seeks to strengthen food security and encourage responsible agricultural practices.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

The proposed platform would use NASA satellite data sources, including Landsat, MODIS, SMAP, GPM, POWER, ECOSTRESS, GRACE-FO, and SRTM. Artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms would be used to analyze environmental information and generate recommendations. Potential development tools include Python for data processing and machine learning, Google Earth Engine for satellite image analysis, and a web-based platform for farmers to interact with the system. The project would primarily rely on digital tools and satellite information rather than specialized physical hardware.

5. How is your project creative?

Our project is creative because it combines artificial intelligence, satellite technology, and local agricultural information in a single tool. Instead of providing general farming recommendations, the platform would generate personalized crop rotation strategies based on the specific conditions of each agricultural parcel. It also connects soil conservation practices with climate information, creating a more comprehensive approach to sustainable agriculture.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered several environmental, agricultural, and technological factors, including:

  • Soil characteristics, pH, and organic matter content.
  • Water availability and historical rainfall patterns.
  • Temperature variations and solar radiation.
  • Droughts, heavy rainfall, and soil erosion.
  • Vegetation health and water stress.
  • Nutritional requirements of different crops.
  • Compatibility between consecutive crops.
  • Agricultural productivity and water consumption.
  • Soil conservation and climate adaptation practices.
  • Accessibility and ease of use for farmers.
